_doc: Per-chassis orientation corrections, applied by export-roster.py.
WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT AN ALGORITHM: a vehicle's NOSE cannot be
determined reliably from geometry. Two independent measures were tried
across the roster and disagreed with each other — a head/visor part-Z
test called 22 of 28 reversed, a taper-and-height asymmetry test called
16 reversed, and the two sets did not match. The robot pose IS
determinable (feet-to-head gives up, a left/right limb pair gives
forward, and all 28 measure +Y up and within 11 degrees of -Z), but a
car is roughly symmetric front to back and the asymmetries that do
exist are small and contradictory.
So: the engine declares rather than guesses. Put a chassis in here and
its whole strip is turned by `yaw` degrees about Y.
yaw   turn the WHOLE strip, keeping vehicle and robot consistent with
each other. Use when both modes face the same wrong way.
turn  spend the rotation ACROSS the fold instead: the vehicle keeps
its facing, the robot lands on the turned one, and the poses
between carry the difference. Use when the vehicle looks right
and the robot does not, or the reverse.
Both are in degrees. Empty means the export is unmodified, which is the
current state — nothing here is a guess I could not verify.
